dimension_justifications.soundness: The conditional linear-band and capped paired-difference arguments are stated clearly, and the snapshot records a targeted nonnegative-self-comparator repair (E12). However, the empirical frontier and allocation claims remain snapshot-reported rather than end-to-end reproducible, and the central deployment premise is only evaluated on constructed class-mixture grids rather than a natural shift with a within-group invariance audit.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper defines regret, commit, abstain, and the exact/asymptotic boundary early, and Table 1 is helpful. Still, its central message is materially diluted by the M1/M2/M2.5/M3/M3.5 taxonomy and two allocation stories. The main result table foregrounds an asymptotic paired normal endpoint while the exact paired theorem's Maurer--Pontil endpoint appears separately, and the abstract's stronger 'exactly on turnover-skew mixtures' wording has no corresponding per-mixture display.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The most credible contribution is the conditional, finite-sample mixture-indexed regret gate for a fixed candidate pool, with an explicit abstention boundary. The allocation and surrogate material is cautiously framed as descriptive/diagnostic, but is narrow and does not establish a safe allocation policy or natural subgroup-mix turnover value; this limits current significance beyond the conditional construction.

paper_summary: The paper studies choosing among fixed classifiers when only subgroup mixture weights may change. It uses calibration data to select by point estimate and commits only when an absolute or paired regret upper bound is below tolerance tau; otherwise it abstains. It proves simultaneous linear and paired certificates over the mixture simplex, reports constructed class-mixture diagnostics on four carriers, and adds descriptive label-budget allocation and width-surrogate analyses.
strongest_verified_contribution: Under the explicitly stated fixed-within-subgroup-risk and calibration assumptions, Theorem 1 gives a plainly stated paired, mixture-simplex regret certificate for any data-dependent chosen candidate; the E12 audit also documents why adding the nonnegative cap repairs the historical self-comparator boundary without changing nonnegative-tau gate decisions.
strengths: The opening problem, regret definition, and distinction between a certificate outcome and deployment utility are unusually explicit (Abstract; Secs. 1--2).

The manuscript repeatedly separates exact finite-sample certificates from the normal/CLT diagnostic and separates descriptive allocation outcomes from inferential claims (Table 1; Secs. 5--7; Limitations).
The taxonomy table and theorem-to-policy progression make the intended M2/M2.5 decision rule recoverable despite a dense topic set.
Limitations acknowledge the missing natural temporal/geographic validation, within-group covariate shift, absent fallback cost, and missing M3 per-seed records.
questions: Can the authors make one exact paired certificate endpoint the main empirical result, then visually connect its certificate value, selection, commit/abstain decision, and per-mixture observed diagnostic?

Does 'abstaining exactly on turnover-skew mixtures where forced point-estimate selection has higher observed regret' mean set equality, or only a descriptive association? Please supply the defining set and a table/plot, or narrow the abstract wording.

Will the authors provide a one-command manifest verifier and repair the declared root snapshot hash so a reviewer can authenticate the frozen package before relying on its snapshot-reported numerical tables?
Can the claimed practical scope remain explicitly restricted to constructed label-prior shifts until the planned natural time/region and conditional-invariance audit is executed?

issues.location: Abstract, lines 38--55; Table 1; Secs. 5--7 and Tables 2--5 (PDF pp. 1--8)
issues.observed_evidence: The paper presents five labels (M1, M2/P2, M2.5/P3, M3, M3.5). Its central exact paired result is Theorem 1 and the Table 3 MPB rate 0.260, but Table 2, named 'Main endpoints,' pairs the absolute exact gate with the more favorable 0.503 asymptotic normal variant. Secs. 6--7 then introduce allocation contrasts and a surrogate that the paper correctly says is neither the actual UCB objective nor a policy. No early decision-flow figure connects the selected model, the paired UCB, tau, and commit/abstain across w.
issues.why_it_matters: A reviewer can recover each qualification, but must actively reconstruct which result is the paper's deployable contribution. This blurs the paper identity and makes the scope disclaimers read as competing stories rather than a coherent argument; it also risks overemphasizing the asymptotic endpoint despite correct labels.
issues.required_fix: Choose the exact paired M2.5 gate as the explicit main empirical endpoint, consolidate Tables 2--3 or redesign them so exact and asymptotic rows are directly comparable, and add a compact early schematic or one-dimensional mixture illustration showing point-estimate selection, paired certificate gating, and abstention. Move or compress the surrogate/allocation story unless it directly supports that primary decision object.
issues.verification_test: A reader should be able, from the abstract, one figure/table, and Sec. 5 alone, to identify the deployed rule, its exact certificate, its commitment rate, and why the normal result is non-primary without consulting Secs. 6--7 or the appendix.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment is required for the restructuring; retain the existing exact/asymptotic labels and reported rates.

Do not strengthen empirical claims until the missing replay materials are supplied.
issues.verification_test: Run the shipped verifier on a fresh copy; it must reproduce the declared root hash and report the per-table evidence availability shown in the manuscript or reviewer-safe evidence summary.

issues.location: Title; Abstract, lines 27--55; Sec. 2 Assumption 1; Sec. 5.2; Sec. 9 Limitations; evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv C05--C06; protocol/decisive_experiment_protocol.md
issues.observed_evidence: The observed evaluations use classes as subgroups and pre-registered constructed mixture grids on four public classification carriers. The supplied evidence explicitly records no natural temporal/geographic mixture-shift validation, no within-group invariance audit, and no measured fallback cost; E11 is a planned but unexecuted protocol. The text acknowledges these limitations, but the title and abstract frame a deployment-turnover problem before the constructed nature of the tests becomes visible.
issues.why_it_matters: This is the decision-relevant external-validity boundary. The conditional theorem may still be useful, but current evidence does not establish that the fixed class-conditional-risk premise holds in the intended deployment setting or that abstention improves operator utility.
issues.required_fix: Either execute the locked natural time/region, conditional-invariance, and precommitted-fallback protocol, or foreground 'constructed label-prior mixtures under a conditional turnover assumption' in the abstract and title/introduction framing, with the practical deployment language kept explicitly conditional.
issues.verification_test: For a claim of deployment relevance, verify that the new study uses source-only FIT/CAL, target-only OUTER, a predeclared subgroup/candidate setup, conditional-loss invariance audit with uncertainty, and a fixed fallback/cost sensitivity record; otherwise verify that the abstract no longer implies this evidence exists.
issues.evidence_needed: E11 executed with its required immutable data version, split/config/environment record, and target conditional-invariance and fallback endpoints.

issues.location: Abstract, lines 41--44; Sec. 5.2, especially Table 2 and 'Descriptive abstention pattern' (PDF p. 5)
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract says the method is 'abstaining exactly on turnover-skew mixtures where forced point-estimate selection has higher observed regret.' In the main text, the directly displayed support is the aggregate comparison of abstained versus committed forced-pick regret (0.0044 versus 0.00001); it neither defines 'turnover-skew' nor establishes set equality between abstentions and higher-regret mixtures.
issues.why_it_matters: 'Exactly' is stronger and less interpretable than the aggregate diagnostic the reader sees, and it can be mistaken for an optimal-abstention or utility result that the paper elsewhere rejects.
issues.required_fix: Replace 'exactly' with a qualified aggregate statement, or define the mixture subset and add the corresponding per-mixture contingency display with an explicit non-utility caveat.
issues.verification_test: The abstract statement must be directly recoverable from a cited main-text table/figure and must not imply optimal abstention, measured fallback utility, or a natural-shift result.
issues.evidence_needed: Existing per-row E03 records may suffice if they support the asserted relationship; otherwise only the weaker aggregate wording is justified.

ethics_concerns: No direct human-subject, privacy, or harmful-deployment violation is evidenced in the frozen package. The practical risk is epistemic: a finite-sample certificate conditional on fixed within-subgroup risk should not be represented as a deployment guarantee without the missing natural-shift and fallback-cost audits.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control, following the supplied frozen-snapshot protocol and rubric.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A manifest verifier that reproduces the declared root hash, plus reviewer-safe raw/config/split/environment material for all main numerical tables.

A preregistered natural temporal and geographic shift study with target conditional-loss invariance audit, exact primary gate, and fixed fallback/cost sensitivity endpoints (the supplied E11 protocol).
A focused main-paper presentation that makes the exact paired gate rather than the asymptotic diagnostic and surrogate the unmistakable primary contribution.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: A corrected manifest calculation showing that listed file bytes or the manuscript/PDF no longer match the frozen entries.
A replay revealing nonzero committed violations, invalid split isolation, or a mismatch between the stated paired certificate and its implementation.
Natural-shift conditional-loss audits that detect material within-group change while deployment-safe claims remain unchanged.
review_limitations: I reviewed only the provided frozen round-2 submission and did not inspect previous rounds, author plans, or external repository history.
The assessment of numerical results is limited to the included artifacts and their declared provenance; I did not treat unexecuted planned work as evidence.
I inspected PDF text and source for layout/consistency, but did not alter or rebuild the frozen manuscript.
